tasks.entryDescription: Hook-walk probabilistic proof; determinant evaluation; representation-theoretic dimension formula; bijective/combinatorial proofs.
tasks.currentSketch: Run the Greene–Nijenhuis–Wilf hook walk from an outside corner: at each cell choose uniformly among cells strictly to its left or above in its hook, then move to the chosen cell. Compute the probability of terminating at each removable corner; the resulting recurrence matches the tableau count f^λ=|λ|!/∏h(c), with the hook factors emerging from transition probabilities.

tasks.entryName: Compactness theorem of first-order logic
tasks.entryDescription: Syntactic proof via completeness/Henkin construction; semantic proof via ultraproducts; topological proof using compactness of a product space.
tasks.currentSketch: Assume every finite subset of the first-order theory T has a model. Expand the language in countably many stages by fresh constants witnessing each existential formula, while preserving finite satisfiability. The resulting Henkin theory has a model built from closed terms modulo provable equality: interpret functions on term classes and relations by membership in the theory. Its reduct satisfies T.

tasks.currentSketch: Let I be the finite subsets of Γ and choose a model A_i of each i. For each finite i let J_i={j∈I:i⊆j}; these cones have the finite-intersection property, so extend their generated filter to an ultrafilter U. In the ultraproduct Π_i A_i/U, for each φ∈Γ the indices whose structures satisfy φ include J_{ {φ} }, hence form a U-large set. Łoś’s theorem gives that the ultraproduct satisfies every φ.

tasks.entryName: Cyclotomic polynomial Φₙ(x) is irreducible over Q
tasks.entryDescription: Eisenstein after substituting x+1 for prime-power cases plus induction/divisibility; Galois action on primitive roots; reduction modulo a prime and Frobenius.
tasks.currentSketch: Let f be the minimal polynomial over Q of a primitive n-th root ζ. For a prime p∤n, suppose ζ^p is not a conjugate; let g be its distinct minimal polynomial. Then f and g are distinct monic integer factors of X^n−1. Modulo p, Frobenius gives the relevant pth-power relation between roots, forcing a repeated factor of X^n−1; this is impossible because p∤n makes X^n−1 square-free mod p. Thus ζ and ζ^p are conjugate. Factoring any a coprime to n into primes not dividing n and iterating shows every ζ^a is conjugate to ζ, so Φ_n is irreducible over Q.

tasks.routeTitle: reduction modulo a prime and Frobenius
tasks.currentSketch: For p∤n, every root α of Φ_n over F_p is a primitive n-th root: otherwise it would also be a root of X^d−1 for a proper divisor d|n, contradicting separability of X^n−1. Frobenius α↦α^p has orbit length ord_n(p), so each irreducible factor of Φ_n mod p has degree ord_n(p). Consequently Φ_n mod p is irreducible exactly when p mod n generates (Z/nZ)^×. This is a conditional modular criterion; such a prime need not exist for every n.
